newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keen buying fuels Singapore stocks to a firm close.
newsitem.headline: Keen buying fuels Singapore stocks to a firm close.

text.p: Brisk buying of selected blue-chips, namely banking stocks, and small capitalised stocks boosted the Singapore stock market to a firmer close on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said interest was evident mainly from overseas fund managers who were adjusting their portfolio of regional stocks.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 14.19 points up at 2,219.88. Total turnover was a healthy 196.49 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 201 to 167.
The SES Finance index ended 4.77 points up at 518.68 points.
Interior design and furniture firm Nobel topped the actives with 46.6 million shares. Dealers said heavy short-selling pushed the stock to end Singapore $0.10 (US$0.07) up at S$0.635.
Precision engineering specilist Armstrong Industrial Corp saw 5.46 million shares traded after several broking houses put a buy recommendation on it. It ended up S$0.025 at S$0.505.
SingTel eased S$0.06 to S$3.32, dampened by news it has cut its phone rates.
Singapore Press Foreign led gainers, rising S$0.80 to S$27.00 while Jurong Shipyard extended its losses, shedding S$0.25 to S$6.80.
